historical: The PR 36-38 Stage 4 comparisons are the committed outputs of black-box Cells 36-38 (arbiters of 2026-11-06, meta_ebm/2). They are neither re-read nor replaced; their upstream (the legacy notebook Stage 2, isotonic Stage 1 LR) differs from PR 39's, so no number is compared across the two.
limitations: The test split is previously exposed (PR 38 protocol section 15; contract L1, section 12). Every result is descriptive and informs no calibration, bin, selector, threshold or Stage 4 setting.
Retained-only metrics are conditional on each arbiter's own confidence rule. Two arbiters retain different rows, so the registered with-abstention differences compare different populations.

The registered abstention cut maximises F2 on retained training rows subject to retained coverage >= 0.50 (shared.stage4.tune_min_confidence). F2 = 5TP / (5TP + 4FN + FP) has no TN term, so retaining a true negative never raises it. Both confidences are threshold-relative (|p - t|, or the GLASS Arbiter's weighted |p - t|), so with t below 0.5 a negative decision's confidence is bounded by t and a positive one's by 1 - t. Abstention can therefore fall mostly on correct negatives. Retained recall and precision then rise while retained accuracy falls, and retained recall overstates the share of all positives found (effective recall). The accounting block and its decomposition report this per cell. The protocol is not changed.
The coverage floor binds on training rows only. Test coverage is reported against it per cell and can fall below it.

The GLASS Arbiter's score is a weighted average of upstream probabilities, not a calibrated probability: it supports ROC-AUC and PR-AUC as a ranking, not calibration metrics. Meta-XGB decides and abstains in its raw, class-weighted space; its calibrated probability is reported separately.

The existing metric code reports a zero-denominator precision, recall or F-score as 0 (zero_division=0, the bootstrap's _prf). The GLASS Arbiter's own stored metrics (compute_metrics) store ROC-AUC 0.5 on a one-class population. The accounting block reports both as undefined, and the record checks that no stored value of the four arbiters relies on either convention.
The bootstrap resamples test rows with the models fixed: it does not reflect training variability.

Stage 2's role is descriptive (F10). Test-side route rates are not checks of the obligations, which bind at fit on training OOF. The PR 38 Tier 2 complementarity results remain tied to the historical upstream and are not compared with these.
Stage 4 stacking keeps an indirect upstream dependence (contract L7, F39).
